# Implementation

## Changed behavior

The intake boundary now accepts `formatVersion: 2` for both `submitOrder` and `importOrders`. Omitted `formatVersion` and numeric `1` continue to use the original version 1 rules. Any other version selector is rejected as `invalid_order`.

Version 2 rows require the existing `id` and `customerId` rules, plus `amount.decimal`. Decimal text is validated without floating point arithmetic, converted exactly to integer cents, and bounded to 1 through 1,000,000 cents. `amount.currency` defaults only when omitted; when present it must be exactly `USD`.

Version 2 `shipOn` may be omitted, in which case the trusted call `context.receivedOn` is used. When present, `shipOn` must be an object with integer `year`, `month`, and `day` forming a real Gregorian date from 2000 through 2099, and it is normalized to `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Accepted version 2 orders are saved and returned in the same canonical shape as version 1: `id`, `customerId`, `amountCents`, `currency`, `shipOn`, and `receivedOn`. Wire-only fields such as `formatVersion`, `amount`, and date components are not stored or exposed.

## Affected call paths

`submitOrder` now passes the intake context into `parseOrder`, allowing the parser to apply the version 2 date default before any repository operation.

`importOrders` uses the same context-aware parser for each row. Batch ordering, partial success behavior, duplicate handling, and summaries remain driven by `saveOrder` results, so only completed `201` saves contribute to `acceptedCount`, `totalAcceptedCents`, and `latestShipOn`.

`saveOrder` and `getOrder` were not changed. Duplicate detection still reads existing canonical records before saving, and reads never rewrite stored data.

## Justified deviations

The existing project keeps shared public types in `src/types.ts`; this implementation preserved that structure to keep the change focused and avoid unrelated file churn.

`bun run typecheck` failed before invoking TypeScript with Bun's internal `CouldntReadCurrentDirectory` error in this workspace. Compiler validation was run with `bun ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` and also directly through `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`; both passed.

## Remaining limitations

No storage migration, damaged-record repair, retry protocol, clock use, currency conversion, or batch transaction behavior was added. Those remain outside the documented scope.

evidence.explanation: currency is an optional recognized field on the amount object.
